lane: B4 — the multiplayer lobby / READY screen: the leaked debug strip, and the race-coloured READY button
owner_item: "The ready in multiplayer sucks… What the shit is that 'host pc=0 mode=hosting'? Just take that off. You leave the 'Room 1/4', 'ready 0/1' or whatever, 'share the code', 'waiting for players', and then READY. That's it. And your READY should be the color of your race — once you click it. It's just a little extra thing to look cool."
root_cause:
TWO SEPARATE THINGS, both confirmed by reading the code.

(1) THE ORANGE LINE IS UNCONDITIONAL IN PRODUCTION. It is the S46 "host-side diagnostic strip", composed in `main.ts` inside the per-frame lobby block and printed by `lobbyScreen.updateHostDiagnostics`. Its only gate is `showLobby && session.netTransport !== null` (main.ts:3727) plus `world.isHost` (main.ts:3798). There is NO `?debug=1` check, no `import.meta.env.DEV` check, no env check anywhere on this path. It was instrumentation written for a 2-peer smoke test in S46 ("User screenshots this strip during 2-peer smoke → empirical root cause", main.ts:3797) and it was never taken back out. Its colour — `fill: 0xffaa44` at lobbyScreen.ts:404 — is exactly the orange/amber in his screenshot, and `MAX_PLAYERS = 4` (constants.ts:87) is why line 1 reads "Room 1/4". Field-by-field: `pc=` transport peerCount; `mode=` / `hc=` / `bv=` from `lobbyScreen.getDebugState()` (lobbyScreen.ts:686 — lobby mode, the hostConnected latch, beginButton.visible); `gm=` `world.gameMode`; `gs=` `world.gameState`; `[nostr:7/7 torrent:2/2]` from `formatStrategySummary(td.strategies)` (net/strategySummary.ts:23).

⭐ `gm=solo` IS NOT A BUG AND IS NOT "SOLO MODE". `world.gameMode` is initialised `'solo'` (state/world.ts:414) and is only rewritten by START_GAME, which is what leaves the lobby. Every lobby on every path prints `gm=solo`. Do not chase it.

(2) A SECOND, IDENTICAL STRIP EXISTS FOR THE OTHER PLAYER AND HE HAS NOT SEEN IT YET. main.ts:3741 `lobbyScreen.updateDiagnostics(...)` prints `sync a/b seq=… kind=… applyErr=… gs=LOBBY [nostr:7/7 …]` in 13px grey (`fill: 0x777777`, lobbyScreen.ts:391) to any JOINER with peerCount > 0 — same class of leak, same absence of a gate, one row higher on screen. Fixing only the orange one leaves the joiner's screen ugly for the person he invited.

(3) THE RACE COLOUR IS AVAILABLE AT LOBBY TIME — the feature is NOT blocked. Race is chosen in the lobby (the S161 P6 seat-rack picker), rides `LOBBY_PRESENCE` as `RosterEntry.raceId`, and `RosterEntry.color` is literally `RACE_COLORS[raceId]` and nothing else (net/lobbyRoster.ts:113). That reaches the screen already: `lobbyView` puts it on `SeatView.color` for the seat with `isYou === true` (lobbyStateMachine.ts:459-462), and `applyView` already holds that array as `v.seats`. `paintReadyButton` (lobbyScreen.ts:993) simply never looks at it — it hardcodes `0x9bff3b` / `0x163a16` for ready and `0xaaaaaa` / `0x222222` for idle. Even the pre-roster fallback is safe: it uses `PLAYER_COLORS[i]`, and `races.test.ts:34` pins `RACE_COLORS[ALL_RACES[i]] === PLAYER_COLORS[i]`, so the fallback colour IS the default race's colour.

evidence.why_it_matters: THIS IS THE EXACT LINE ON HIS SCREENSHOT, character for character. The enclosing `if` tests `world.isHost` and nothing else; the enclosing block (main.ts:3727) tests `showLobby && session.netTransport !== null`. There is no debug flag, no DEV gate, no query-param seam on this path — it is unconditional in the shipped build.

The strip's own docblock says what it is: throwaway state-discovery instrumentation for one S46 bug hunt, designed to be screenshotted. It was never gated and never removed. This is the provenance to quote to him — it is not a feature he was never told about, it is a debugging aid left switched on.

THE SECOND LEAK. Same block, same absence of a gate, shown to any JOINER with peerCount > 0 (main.ts:3734). He screenshotted the host's orange line because he was hosting; the player who joins him sees this grey one. Gating only the orange strip half-fixes the screen.

0xffaa44 is the orange/amber he described, 13px monospace is the 'smaller' he described, and the y-position (+82) puts it under the status line — it matches the screenshot exactly. It defaults to `visible = false`; only `updateHostDiagnostics` with non-empty text turns it on (lobbyScreen.ts:768-775), so gating the CALLER is sufficient and needs no change in this class.

THE SEAM ALREADY EXISTS, IS PURE, IS UNIT-TESTED, AND IS ALREADY IMPORTED BY main.ts (line 149: `import { netStats, netStatsRequested } from './net/netStats.ts';`). Gating both strips behind it costs ZERO new imports, zero new concepts and zero bundle bytes, and the answer to 'how do I get the relay readout back' becomes the same `?debug=1` URL the owner already uses for the debug overlay (main.ts:2371).

ANSWERS THE BLOCKING QUESTION: the seat colour on the wire IS the race colour, derived at construction, for every seat, in the lobby, before the match. `color` is `RACE_COLORS[raceId]` and nothing else. So 'the color of your race' needs no new field, no new wire traffic and no PROTOCOL_VERSION bump — the value is already on the lobby screen.

fix_shape:
FOUR CHANGES. All render-only. No new assets, no wire change, no sim change.

── A · GATE BOTH DIAGNOSTIC STRIPS BEHIND THE SEAM THAT ALREADY EXISTS (recommended over deletion; see owner_ruling_needed #1) ──
In main.ts, hoist one boolean near the top of the module body, beside the existing `?debug=1` block at main.ts:2371:
  `const LOBBY_DIAGNOSTICS = netStatsRequested(window.location.search);`
(`netStatsRequested` is ALREADY imported at main.ts:149 — no new import, no new bundle bytes.) Then:
  · main.ts:3734 — `if (LOBBY_DIAGNOSTICS && !world.isHost && session.netTransport.peerCount() > 0) {`
  · main.ts:3798 — `if (LOBBY_DIAGNOSTICS && world.isHost) {`
Both `else` arms already call `update*Diagnostics('')`, which sets `visible = false` (lobbyScreen.ts:768-774, :795-801) — so the default URL shows NOTHING and `?debug=1` (or `?netstats=1`) restores both strips verbatim. Nothing else changes. Leave the docblocks at main.ts:3729 and :3791 in place and add one line to each saying the strip is now seam-gated and why.
⚠ Compute the boolean ONCE at module scope, not per frame — `window.location.search` inside a 60 Hz ticker is a needless read and the existing `?debug=1` sites all read it once.

── B · THE READY BUTTON WEARS THE RACE COLOUR, ONLY WHEN READY ──
New pure module `src/render/readyButtonPaint.ts` (new file so no other branch's file is touched, and so the decision is unit-testable with NO renderer):
  · `export const READY_IDLE_STROKE = 0xaaaaaa; export const READY_IDLE_FILL = 0x222222;` — today's idle values, unchanged, now named.
  · `export const READY_FALLBACK_COLOR = 0x9bff3b;` — today's green, kept for the one window where the self seat is unknown.
  · `export function selfSeatColor(seats: readonly SeatView[]): number | null` — `seats.find(s => s.occupied && s.isYou)?.color ?? null`. Imports only the `SeatView` TYPE from lobbyStateMachine.ts, so that file is NOT edited.
  · `export function darkenForPlate(color: number): number` — per-channel multiply, `r,g,b → round(c * 0.16)`, mirroring how today's 0x163a16 sits under 0x9bff3b. Pure integer maths, no float accumulator, render-only.
  · `export function readyButtonPaint(selfReady: boolean, raceColor: number | null): { stroke: number; fill: number; label: string }` — idle ⇒ `{ READY_IDLE_STROKE, READY_IDLE_FILL, 'READY?' }`; ready ⇒ `{ raceColor ?? READY_FALLBACK_COLOR, darkenForPlate(that), 'READY ✓' }`.
In lobbyScreen.ts: add `private selfRaceColor: number | null = null;`, have `paintReadyButton()` call `readyButtonPaint(this.selfReady, this.selfRaceColor)` and apply the three values (identical Graphics calls, only the literals move), and clear `selfRaceColor = null` in `reset()` alongside `selfReady = false`.

── C · THE REPAINT TRIGGER — THIS IS THE HALF THAT WILL BE FORGOTTEN ──
`paintReadyButton` is NOT called from `applyView` today (callers: constructor :463, click :455, resets :655/:1013/:1084). Inside `applyView`'s `if (showReady)` block (lobbyScreen.ts:931), after the tally, add:
  `const nextColor = selfSeatColor(v.seats); if (nextColor !== this.selfRaceColor) { this.selfRaceColor = nextColor; this.paintReadyButton(); }`
`applyView` runs on every real state transition, and `updatePresence` → `lobbyReduce(PRESENCE)` → `rostersEqual` already compares `raceId` per entry (lobbyStateMachine.ts:164, S163 P6), so a race pick reaches here. Without this line the button paints once at construction and a race change never lands — the fix would look done and be dead.

── D · A DEV/E2E READ ACCESSOR, so the one lane that actually renders can assert it ──
Alongside the existing `getStatusText()` / `getSeats()` / `getRoomCode()` accessors (lobbyScreen.ts:710-722), add `getReadyButtonPaint(): { stroke: number; fill: number; label: string; visible: boolean }` and `getDiagnosticsStrips(): { joiner: string; host: string }` (returning `''` when hidden). Cheap, no behaviour, and the only way a Playwright lane can pin either half in a real browser.

⭐ NO-COST ALTERNATIVE IF HE WANTS THE RELAY HEALTH STILL VISIBLE WITHOUT A URL PARAM: the `Test your connection` button already on this screen (lobbyScreen.ts:~505, `onTestConnection` → `showConnectionTestResult`) is the owner-facing version of the same information and prints into its own panel on demand. Point him at it in one sentence rather than building anything.
determinism_risk:
NONE-RENDER-ONLY.

No sim state is read or written. No `Math.random`, no wall clock, no float accumulator enters the sim — `darkenForPlate` is integer channel maths inside the renderer and is never reached from a tick. Nothing is added to `world`, so the four-sites obligation (factory + serialize + hash + worker) does not apply and neither `hashWorldState` nor `hashWorldStateFull` changes.

PROTOCOL_VERSION stays 47 (`src/net/protocol.ts:704`). ⭐ The race colour is ALREADY on the wire and has been since S161 P6: `RosterEntry.color` is `RACE_COLORS[raceId]` (net/lobbyRoster.ts:113) and `raceId` is an additive-optional field already shipped. No new discriminant, no new required field, no new `GameEffect` kind, so none of the four exhaustive switches and no bump. Nothing is sent that was not sent before — the fix only reads what already arrives, which is the "prefer deriving over sending" rule applied for free.

⚠ Two non-determinism-class hazards worth naming instead:
· `LOBBY_DIAGNOSTICS` must be computed ONCE at module scope. Reading `window.location.search` inside the 60 Hz ticker is wasteful and drifts from the existing `?debug=1` sites' pattern.
· If the eventual ruling is DELETE rather than GATE, `lobbyScreen.getDebugState()` (:686), `hostDiagnosticsText` (:176/:402/:663/:768) and possibly `diagnosticsText` become unreferenced. Leaving them is a knip/`npm run build` hazard, and removing them is a wider diff than the gate — which is one more reason the gate is the cheaper answer.
art_cost:
NO-ART. Zero spend, and there is no version of this that needs generation.

· The debug strip is deleted text — negative pixels.
· The READY button is a `Graphics.roundRect().fill().stroke()` drawn procedurally in Pixi every time `paintReadyButton` runs (lobbyScreen.ts:995-999). Changing the two colour literals to values read from `SeatView.color` is a data change to an existing draw call. No atlas, no PNG, no sprite, no tint of an imported texture, no filter, no mask.
· The six race colours are already six integer literals in `RACE_COLORS` (state/races.ts:74-81) and are already pinned equal to `PLAYER_COLORS` by `races.test.ts:34`.
· The dark plate behind the ready state is computed from the race colour by integer multiply, not authored.

ART_PIPELINE.md was read: its subject is stage-1→5 character/tower sheets (owner generates a still → Claude mattes → owner generates clips → `check-clip.mjs` → `build-sprite-atlas.mjs`). None of its stages is entered. veo clips cost ~$20 each (his measurement) and this lane spends $0.
tests_owed:
⚠ NO RENDERER RUNS UNDER VITEST. Nothing in the unit suite instantiates Pixi — `lobbyScreen.test.ts` (380 lines) tests ONLY the pure helpers it re-exports from `lobbyGeometry.ts` and says so in its own header ("WITHOUT spinning up Pixi Application or a DOM environment"). So the unit suite can never prove the button is actually stroked with 0xd73bff on screen, nor that the orange line is gone. Be honest about that split:

WHAT CAN BE PINNED PROPERLY (real behaviour, new file `src/render/readyButtonPaint.test.ts`):
· `readyButtonPaint(false, anyColor)` returns the idle triple and the label `'READY?'` — i.e. the race colour does NOT leak into the idle state (his "once you click it").
· `readyButtonPaint(true, c)` for all six `RACE_COLORS` values returns `stroke === c` and `label === 'READY ✓'`.
· `readyButtonPaint(true, null)` falls back to `READY_FALLBACK_COLOR` (0x9bff3b) — the joiner-before-first-beacon window.
· `darkenForPlate` returns a strictly darker value per channel for all six races, and the result is never equal to the stroke (a plate the same colour as its stroke is an invisible button).
· `selfSeatColor` over a hand-built `SeatView[]`: returns the `isYou && occupied` seat's colour; returns `null` when no seat is `isYou`; ignores an `isYou` seat that is unoccupied.
· A canon-style cross-check: for each seat index i, `selfSeatColor` of a count-based fallback view equals `RACE_COLORS[defaultRaceForSeat(i)]` — this is what makes the pre-roster window correct rather than accidentally correct.

WHAT ONLY A SOURCE-TEXT GUARD CAN REACH (new file `src/render/lobbyDiagnosticsGate.test.ts`), AND ITS LIMIT STATED OUT LOUD:
Read `main.ts` with `readFileSync` and assert MECHANICALLY, in the S182 `s182UiSurfaceGuards.test.ts` style — count the sites, do not just look for one:
· `updateHostDiagnostics(` and `updateDiagnostics(` each appear exactly TWICE in main.ts (one show arm, one clear arm). A third call site fails the test until someone gates it.
· The gate identifier appears on the same `if` as each show arm.
· ⛔ AND THE LIMIT, WRITTEN INTO THE FILE'S DOCBLOCK: **a source-text guard proves a line EXISTS, it cannot prove the line is REACHED** (S182 §2 — a tripwire was green over a live bug twice). This guard cannot tell you the strip is invisible in a browser. Say so in the commit message too.
⚠ Match on substrings with no newline so a CRLF checkout reads the same as LF (the recurring Windows-only false-red; `s182UiSurfaceGuards.test.ts:44` carries the same warning).

THE ONLY LANE THAT ACTUALLY RENDERS — Playwright. `e2e/lobby-construction.spec.ts` already exists and `__SPARK__.lobbyScreen` is already exposed (main.ts:2046) with `getUiPoints` / `getSeats` / `getStatusText`. With accessor D added, an e2e can: open the lobby, assert `getDiagnosticsStrips()` is `{joiner:'', host:''}` on the plain URL and non-empty under `?debug=1`; click QUICK MATCH, click READY via `getUiPoints().readyButton`, and assert `getReadyButtonPaint().stroke` equals the seat's own colour from `getSeats()`. ⚠ Decide the lane deliberately: `e2e:gating` is the shared 720 s lane, `e2e:races` is the slow one, and `src/ci.e2eLanes.test.ts` PINS the spec→lane mapping — adding a spec without updating it turns that test red.

blocked_on:
NOTHING IS BLOCKED. The question the task flagged as potentially fatal — "has the player's race been chosen and synced at lobby time?" — is answered YES, in the code, three ways:

1. The race picker IS a lobby surface. `racePicker.ts` opens from the seat-rack cell, `onPickRace` is a `LobbyScreenCallbacks` member (lobbyScreen.ts:100), and main.ts:1859 handles it: the host writes `session.selfRace` and rebroadcasts, a joiner sends `CLAIM_RACE` and waits.
2. The colour rides the existing lobby presence beacon. `buildLobbyRoster` → `rosterEntryFor` sets `color: RACE_COLORS[raceId]` (net/lobbyRoster.ts:113); `broadcastQmPresence` is the single presence path and calls `onPresence` UNCONDITIONALLY, even with a null transport (net/quickmatchGate.ts:71 — the S162 P1 fix for the owner's "i cant seem to change my player color(race) … it doesnt change"), so the local repaint always happens.
3. It already reaches the screen. main.ts:1693 digests the roster into `SeatPresence`, `lobbyView` projects it onto `SeatView.color` with `isYou` precomputed, and `applyView` already holds that array. `paintReadyButton` just never looks.

⭐ AND THERE IS NO WINDOW WITH NO COLOUR AT ALL. With no roster yet, `lobbyView` falls back to `PLAYER_COLORS[i]` with `raceId: defaultRaceForSeat(i)`, and `races.test.ts:34` pins `RACE_COLORS[ALL_RACES[i]] === PLAYER_COLORS[i]` — so the fallback colour IS the default race's colour, by a tripwire rather than by luck. The one genuine gap is a QUICKMATCH JOINER before its first `LOBBY_PRESENCE`: `fallbackSelfSeat` deliberately claims nothing for a joiner (lobbyStateMachine.ts:435), so `selfSeatColor` returns null for a few frames. That is what `READY_FALLBACK_COLOR` is for, and the change at C repaints the moment the beacon lands.

⛔ AND THE CANON'S DEAD IDEA IS NOT BEING RESURRECTED: seat colour here is RACE IDENTITY ONLY. Nothing in this lane touches castle keeps, and elemental castle keeps stay DECIDED OUT.
